summary: Claude@Stanford’s first year. The site went up in February 2026, and the year ended with the spring hackathon.

winners.title: Crucible
winners.desc: AI validates decisions instead of stress-testing them. Crucible enforces rigorous deliberation through structured stages before delivering a recommendation, making ethical safeguards architectural rather than superficial.

winners.title: ArkSkill
winners.desc: A free web app that generates tailored Claude skill files for humanities researchers, helping them extract structured data from sources like bibliographies, indexes, and tables of contents.

winners.title: Anchor
winners.desc: AI holds the memory so humans can hold each other. An AI companion that preserves patient memories, delivers personalized morning briefs, and reduces caregiver coordination burden for Alzheimer’s families.

mentions.title: Mnemosyne
mentions.desc: A human-AI context management system enabling transparent memory organization and branching conversations for non-linear chat exploration.

mentions.title: EventDrop
mentions.desc: A personalized campus event discovery platform that curates weekly activity recommendations based on user preferences and interests.
